item.title: Russia plotting 'massive strike' during midterms, Zelenskyy warns, urges US to stop Putin
item.description: Zelenskyy says Russia plans a massive attack on Ukraine's energy infrastructure while the world watches Tuesday's U.S. midterm elections unfold.
item.content:encoded:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned Monday that Russia is preparing a "massive attack" on Ukraine centered on Tuesday's midterm elections in the United States, accusing Moscow of seeking to exploit the historical vote to unleash strikes while the world's attention is elsewhere.

The Ukrainian leader's warning came as voters prepared to decide which party controls Congress, a result that could also influence Washington's future response to Russian President Vladimir Putin's almost five-year war in Ukraine.

In a post on X, Zelenskyy went on to urge the Trump administration to increase pressure on Moscow, warning that Russia could exploit the elections to target Ukraine's battered energy infrastructure and supply routes.

DRONE STRIKE SINKS SHIP IN NATO WATERS AS ZELENSKYY WARNS OF LOOMING ‘MASSIVE STRIKE’

"We have intel that Russia is preparing a new massive attack on our country – primarily targeting energy and logistics," Zelenskyy said in his nightly address.

"The assumption is basically that tomorrow the world will be watching the American midterms, and what is happening here in Ukraine, along with our difficulties with air defense and Patriot missiles, will be overlooked."

Zelenskyy's warning came hours after Russian forces struck a school being used to distribute humanitarian aid in Komyshuvakha, a settlement in southeastern Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region.

At least 26 people, including police officers and first responders, were killed, five others were injured and others remained missing, according to the Ukrainian news outlet Ukrainska Pravda.

ZELENSKYY PRESSURES US AND EUROPE FOR MORE 'AIR DEFENSE' ASSISTANCE AMID ONGOING WAR WITH RUSSIA

In his X post, Zelenskyy urged the U.S. and its allies to warn Putin that continued attacks on Ukraine would bring serious economic consequences.

"We need signals from the world to Russia that will make them feel that terror is no good, that it will bring no gains, and that as long as this war continues, their oil will burn, and they will not be able to make money doing business with the world," Zelenskyy warned.

"We must not play games with Russia's oil or gas revenues," he added.

"We must put pressure on Russia in such a way that it has no alternative but to end this war. America can do this."

TRUMP ANNOUNCES IMMEDIATE ENERGY CEASEFIRE BETWEEN RUSSIA AND UKRAINE

President Donald Trump, meanwhile, has sought to negotiate an end to the war with the help of special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, both of whom have been involved in diplomatic efforts with Moscow.

Zelenskyy told Fox News in a Sunday interview that Ukraine would suspend strikes on Russian oil refineries for a month if Washington provided Patriot missile interceptors during the same period, potentially opening the door to diplomacy.

The State Department approved the potential sale of 500 Patriot PAC-3 interceptor missiles to Ukraine for an estimated $2.1 billion, according to Reuters.

The proposed sale could provide a significant boost to Ukraine's air defenses if finalized, although the delivery timeline is uncertain.

TRUMP SAYS US WILL LET UKRAINE MAKE PATRIOT MISSILES IN MAJOR POLICY SHIFT

On Monday, Ukraine also accused Moscow of exploiting a U.S.-backed humanitarian ceasefire in Oleshky, in Ukraine's southern Kherson region, to strengthen Russian military positions.

Nearly 800 people were evacuated during the six-day humanitarian pause, according to first lady Melania Trump, with the White House clarifying that she helped broker the arrangement.

Ukraine's General Staff accused Russian forces of using the humanitarian pause to rotate troops, reinforce their defenses and improve battlefield logistics.

"Under the ceasefire introduced for the humanitarian operation in Oleshky, units of the Defence Forces of Ukraine ensured that the ceasefire was observed and acted exclusively within the framework of the agreements reached," the General Staff said in a statement on X.

"The enemy, by contrast, used the humanitarian pause to improve its positions."

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Woman allegedly raped by illegal alien after Clinton-appointed federal judge ordered his release
item.description: Federal officials said Marcotulio Melendez Diaz, 42, was arrested after allegedly raping a woman Oct. 11 in her Minnesota home.
item.content:encoded:
EXCLUSIVE: An illegal alien who was released from immigration custody by a Clinton-appointed federal judge in August has been charged with allegedly raping a woman inside her own Minnesota home two months later, federal immigration authorities told Fox News.

Marcotulio Melendez Diaz, 42, of Honduras, was working as a handyman on Oct. 11, when he allegedly overpowered and repeatedly raped the resident against her will.

The assault inside the Mounds View home was captured on her indoor surveillance video, officials said.

Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) blasted U.S. District Judge Orlando L. Garcia for ordering his release, arguing that the incident could have been prevented if Melendez Diaz had remained in custody.

ILLEGAL ALIEN ‘PIRATE’ WHO HIJACKED PLANE TO US FREED BY CLINTON-APPOINTED JUDGE

ICE URGES NEW YORK NOT TO RELEASE SALVADORAN NATIONAL ACCUSED OF RAPING 16-YEAR-OLD GIRL ON LONG ISLAND

"This is what happens when activist judges side with criminal illegal aliens over Americans," the agency said in a statement. "ICE arrested him, and an immigration judge ordered his deportation. But a Clinton-appointed federal judge ordered him RELEASED.

"And now an American woman has suffered a horrific crime that could have been PREVENTED."

ICE sources told Fox News that Melendez Diaz was initially apprehended and released at the southern border by the Biden administration in April 2024.

He was arrested again in Minnesota in January 2026, during Operation Metro Surge, and transferred to ICE detention in Texas, according to the officials.

On March 30, an immigration judge issued a deportation order against him, which Melendez Diaz appealed, the authorities said.

FEDERAL JUDGE BLOCKS DEPORTATION OF DOMINICAN ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT SHOT BY ICE DURING NYC ARREST ATTEMPT

While the deportation order was under review, Garcia, a federal judge in the Western District of Texas, ordered his release from ICE custody after granting his habeas petition on due process grounds, finding that his detention had been unlawful or unreasonably prolonged.

The ruling allowed Melendez Diaz to return to Minnesota.

On Oct. 9, Melendez Diaz's appeal was rejected, and the Board of Immigration Appeals issued a deportation order against him.

Just two days after his deportation order became final, he was charged with rape.

Melendez Diaz was charged with felony first-degree criminal sexual penetration involving coercion.

He remains in custody and faces up to 30 years in prison if convicted.

item.title: Florida plane crash victims identified after 9 people killed in fiery wreck
item.description: The Learjet 60 crew reported icing and an overspeed condition before the Austin-to-Bahamas flight plunged into a South Florida neighborhood.
item.content:encoded:
A 20-year-old aspiring airline pilot and a Texas couple traveling with their two young children are among the nine people killed when a private jet plunged into a South Florida neighborhood Sunday.

The Learjet 60 departed Austin-Bergstrom International Airport at about 10:37 a.m. and was headed to North Eleuthera in the Bahamas when it crashed in Palm Beach County shortly before 1 p.m., killing everyone on board.

Federal investigators said Monday that weather conditions are a "major focus" of the investigation after the crew reported icing and moderate turbulence at about 35,000 feet shortly before the jet rapidly lost altitude.

PRIVATE JET WITH 9 PEOPLE ON BOARD CRASHES JUST MILES FROM MAR-A-LAGO

The National Transportation Safety Board also said there are preliminary indications that the aircraft may have begun breaking apart before impact.

The cause of the crash has not been determined.

INVESTIGATORS ZERO IN ON POSSIBLE CAUSE OF WISCONSIN PLANE CRASH THAT KILLED 6

As investigators work to determine what caused the deadly crash, details are beginning to emerge about some of the nine people who were on board.

Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras was an aspiring commercial pilot from Palm Beach County who earned her private pilot's license at 17, before she got her driver's license. Filgueiras trained through her high school's aviation academy and later graduated from American Flyers flight school.

Jeff Gregory, 55, was the pilot in charge, the New York Post reported.

In a joint statement, the families remembered Adam and Helen for their "warmth, generosity and gift for making people feel welcome," saying their relationship was "the love affair that will last forever."

Robinson was CEO and co-founder of Retention.com and also led RB2B and Moltsets.

Retention.com, RB2B and Moltsets issued the following statement following Robinson's death:

"We are heartbroken by the loss of Adam Robinson, our CEO and co-founder, his wife Helen and their two young children, who died in a tragic plane crash in Palm Beach County, Florida, on November 1, 2026.

"Adam was much more than our CEO. He was a friend, a mentor and a bold, outspoken leader who lived life to the fullest. He cared deeply about the people around him and brought energy and conviction to everything he built. His loss is deeply felt across our team and the tech community, as we collectively mourn this significant loss.

"Our hearts are with Adam and Helen’s family and loved ones, and with everyone affected by the crash. We ask that their privacy be respected during this difficult time.

"Our immediate focus at Retention.com, RB2B, and Moltsets is supporting our employees and Adam and Helen’s family. We are grateful for the kindness and support extended to them and our team."

Helen Sharp was an entrepreneur, potter and public relations company owner who was traveling with her husband, Adam Robinson, and their children.

Her family remembered Helen and Adam as devoted parents whose generosity touched those around them, saying their loss "will be felt deeply by all those who loved them and who they loved in return."

Four-year-old Emma Robinson was traveling with her parents, Adam Robinson and Helen Sharp, and her younger brother, Charlie.

Emma and Charlie "were the light of their lives," the families said in a joint statement.

The families remembered Charlie and Emma as the center of their parents' lives.

Upper Jet, which operated the Learjet, declined to confirm the identity of the captain when contacted by Fox News Digital, instead referring questions about the crash to federal investigators.

"We would like to provide our condolences to everyone affected by the catastrophic event of yesterday, November 1, 2026," Upper Jet Director of Operations Thomas Noetzel said in a statement. "Our hearts go out to everyone impacted by this tragedy."

Noetzel said the company is cooperating with local, state and federal authorities and that information about the crash would come from the NTSB and other authorities.

item.title: Scientists discover potentially massive dwarf planet candidate hiding beyond Pluto
item.description: Object 2026 ED138 was spotted beyond Pluto using observations from the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, and scientists say it could be among the largest dwarf planets ever found.
item.content:encoded:
A powerful new telescope has discovered a dwarf planet candidate beyond Pluto — and scientists say it could be among the largest of its kind ever found in the reaches of our solar system.

The discovery, announced Oct. 27, was made using observations from the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, a newly operational facility located on a mountaintop in Chile.

The observatory, jointly funded by the U.S. National Science Foundation and the Department of Energy's Office of Science, began its 10-year survey of the sky in June 2026, using the world's largest digital camera to search for previously unseen objects.

TREASURE HUNTER STRIKES GOLD WITH 1,000-YEAR-OLD DISCOVERY LINKED TO 'HAND OF GOD'

Researchers identified the object as 2026 ED138. They estimated it measures between 370 and 930 miles across.

"If confirmed, ED138 would be among the largest dwarf planets ever discovered in this region of the Solar System," the observatory said in a statement.

On Oct. 13, astronomer Matthew Holman was using computer software he developed with colleague Kevin Napier to search through telescope data collected earlier this year when he spotted the object.

"Using this method, Holman uncovered ED138, and he immediately noticed that its brightness and distance indicated that it is unusually large," the observatory said.

PUZZLING SOUND IN BACKYARD LEADS HOMEOWNER TO MASSIVE 1,000-YEAR-OLD TREASURE

In a statement, Holman described his reaction as "one of excited disbelief."

He added, "Objects like this are very rare, so I immediately started checking whether I or the code had done something wrong." 

ED138 is currently located about 4.3 billion miles from the sun, farther away than Pluto, which orbits the sun at an average distance of about 3.7 billion miles.

Scientists classify ED138 as a trans-Neptunian object, meaning it orbits the sun beyond Neptune, the farthest planet in our solar system.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

As for why the object had not been discovered sooner, officials said it was hiding in a crowded region of the sky near the Milky Way, where millions of stars made it difficult for earlier telescopes to detect.

"Rubin Observatory’s regular and continuous monitoring of the entire Southern Hemisphere sky, combined with powerful algorithms that sift through millions to billions of points of light to identify those corresponding to small moving objects, enabled the team to spot ED138 within the crowded field," the statement added.

Looking ahead, scientists hope to conduct further observations of ED138 to determine its exact size and whether it qualifies as a dwarf planet.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

"If confirmed as a dwarf planet, ED138 would join a very small family of worlds," Holman said in a statement.

"Rubin will image the whole southern sky again and again for 10 years, so any others hiding in the places earlier surveys skipped are now within reach."

A dwarf planet is a celestial body that orbits the sun and is large enough to be nearly round; yet unlike a full-sized planet, it shares its orbital region with other objects it has not gravitationally cleared away.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Pluto was considered the ninth planet in our solar system after its discovery in 1930, but was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.

The newly identified dwarf planet candidate is among several recent discoveries shedding light on the mysteries of our solar system.

Earlier this year, scientists revealed that a meteorite that crashed through the roof of a New Jersey home in 2024 contained some of the chemical building blocks of life and was among the rarest space rocks ever recovered.

At the time, researchers said the meteorite contained material dating back more than 4.5 billion years.

item.title: Spike Lee hopes the Knicks won't visit the White House, warns owner 'can’t force them'
item.description: Spike Lee says he hopes the New York Knicks refuse to visit the White House, claiming owner James Dolan cannot force players to meet President Donald Trump.
item.content:encoded:
Director Spike Lee told Variety he hopes the New York Knicks will refuse to meet with President Donald Trump, as other teams have done after winning championships.

The Knicks won the 2026 NBA Finals by defeating the San Antonio Spurs 4-1 in the championship series in June, ending a 53-year title drought for the franchise. Lee, a devoted Knicks fan and critic of Trump, was asked by Variety's Marlow Stern about reports that some players did not want to visit the White House and would rather skip the longstanding tradition.

"Apparently, the team owner, James Dolan, who we know is a Trump pal, is trying to force them to visit the White House, but the team doesn’t want to," Stern told Lee.

KNICKS OWNER CONFIRMS CHAMPIONSHIP CELEBRATION INVITE TO WHITE HOUSE WHILE SEAHAWKS VISIT ON BACK BURNER

"He can’t force them!" Lee replied. "It’s been years since the last NBA team has gone. They’re not going. I hope they don’t go! I hope they don’t go."

"Trump also messed up Game 3 of the Finals for the Knicks," Stern argued. "They’d won 13 playoff games in a row until Dolan invited Trump to the game and ruined their mojo."

"That was not just an accident!" Lee responded.

They were referring to how Trump, a native New Yorker and longtime Knicks fan, was invited to attend the game at Madison Square Garden by Dolan. The Spurs won the game that day, and many New Yorkers, including "The View" co-host Sunny Hostin, blamed the Knicks’ loss on Trump’s attendance.

CARDI B CLAIMS DONALD TRUMP’S ATTENDANCE BROUGHT A 'DARK' ENERGY TO NBA FINALS GAME 3

Elizabeth Pipko, host of "Made in America with Elizabeth Pipko" and a former Republican National Committee national spokesperson, told Fox News Digital, "Of course, none of these players should ever be forced to do something they don't want to do. But I think there's a much bigger lesson here, especially for young Americans, and it's one Stephen A. Smith articulated very well after facing criticism for having dinner with President Trump."

"You don't have to agree with the president, you don't even have to like him," she continued. "But he is the President of the United States. And if you genuinely care about bringing Americans together, finding solutions, or improving the lives of people in your community, you have to be willing to sit down with people you disagree with."

"This is a lesson that’s incredibly important for young men to learn," Pipko added. "These are individuals who have large followings and should be focusing on inspiring the next generation and teaching them about what matters. Spike Lee's position puts political opposition ahead of an opportunity for dialogue, change, or opportunity. Nothing gets accomplished by staying home, refusing to engage, and acting as though you're somehow morally superior to people who disagree with you."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Fox News Digital reached out to representatives for the Knicks and the White House for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: NHL and Fanatics unveil 'Hometown Remix' jerseys celebrating local culture for all 32 teams
item.description: The NHL and Fanatics unveiled Hometown Remix special edition jerseys for all teams, with three clubs debuting their new threads on Monday night.
item.content:encoded:
Every team in the NHL just got a jersey upgrade on Monday, as the league and Fanatics unveiled "Hometown Remix," a league-wide special edition uniform, apparel and headwear program which "uniquely and authentically celebrates the fans, fabric and local culture of each NHL team and the cities the call home."

The NHL and Fanatics, which took over as the official on-ice uniform and authentic outfitter for the league ahead of the 2024-25 season, have worked together for the past two years developing each Hometown Remix connection.

"Few symbols in sports carry the history, pride, and emotional connection of an NHL sweater," NHL senior executive vice president and chief partnership and club strategy officer, Brian Jennings, said in a press release. "Hometown Remix builds on that legacy in a fresh and authentic way, celebrating the fans, culture and communities that make each NHL market unique.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"Together with Fanatics and our clubs, we’ve created designs that are rooted in local identity and tell a story about the cities and fans they represent. We’re incredibly excited to bring the program to life and see that passion reflected both on the ice and in the stands."

On the ice, the Florida Panthers, Chicago Blackhawks and San Jose Sharks will debut their new threads on Monday night, while each club will wear their respective Hometown Remix uniforms several times throughout the remainder of the season.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Designed from scratch, the NHL and Fanatics aimed to get details like local landmarks, motifs and culture more involved when creating the jerseys for each team.

For example, the Blackhawks have a vivid green base with the current logo and gold shoulder patches. Each sleeve features four debossed six-pointed stars – a nod to Chicago’s city flag.

Then, the Panthers’ jersey takes cues from your favorite graphic beach tee, with a front crest showcasing a remixed version of the throwback Panthers’ shoulder patch logo.

From the Winnipeg Jets’ full aurora borealis scene on the hem to the Boston Bruins having a brown jersey for the first time in more than 100 years, the league made sure to be grounding each look into something recognizable by each rabid fan base.

"Hometown Remix represents the most exciting initiative our team has designed and delivered with our partners since we hit the ice wit the NHL in 2024," Dom Fillion, vice president of creative design for Fanatics, said in a press release. "What makes this program so special is the collaboration with each club and together leaning into the history, culture, fabric and identity of every city and fan base to make sure these felt as authentic and personal as possible. We can’t wait to see them worn by the teams on the ice and the fans in the stands all season long."

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

This marks the first-ever league-wide program following this partnership, but Fanatics had previously designed special edition uniforms for several of the league’s marquee events , including the 4 Nations Face-Off, NHL Winter Classic, NHL Stadium Series, NHL Heritage Classic and the upcoming 2027 All-Star festivities. They also worked with several teams on their anniversary and centennial jerseys.

item.title: BOBBY BURACK: The anti-white resistance is already beginning for Cooper Flagg
item.description: Cooper Flagg's rise as a 19-year-old Dallas Mavericks star is sparking a heated racial debate after ex-NBA player Charlie Villanueva's comments.
item.content:encoded:
Dallas Mavericks forward Cooper Flagg is 19 years old and already one of the best basketball players in the world.

Last week, ESPN analyst Jeremy Lin called him "generational" and said he and Victor Wembanyama could become the NBA’s next great rivalry.

Flagg has also drawn favorable comparisons to LeBron James at the same age, including from Brian Windhorst.

"In my view, Cooper is better at defense than LeBron was at the same age. I don’t even think it’s debatable," Windhorst said.

"There were defensive plays LeBron made at that age. He certainly would get into passing lanes, he certainly would block shots, he was a defensive playmaker, but Cooper is better defensively, empirically; I don’t think that’s debatable."

Flagg is averaging 27 points, six rebounds and seven assists during his second season.

A phenom of Flagg’s caliber should be a gift to the NBA as some of its biggest stars, including LeBron James, Steph Curry and Kevin Durant, approach the end of their careers. Instead, his rise may expose the worst instincts in sports.

Cooper Flagg is White. For some members of the basketball community, that is a problem. Former NBA player Charlie Villanueva is one of them.

Villanueva discussed Flagg’s rising stardom on the "To The Baha" podcast last week. According to Villanueva, Flagg cannot become the face of the NBA because of his skin color.

"This might sound crazy, but I don’t think in 2026 a White dude could be, I’m gonna be real, could be the face of the league, if I’m being honest," Villanueva said. "Because it’s a Black league, right?"

EMBRACE OF WEMBY AS FACE OF THE NBA PROVES RESISTANCE TOWARD JOKIC WAS ALWAYS RACIAL | BOBBY BURACK

He then argued that a White player cannot become the best player in the NBA.

"When is the last time we’ve seen a White man be the face of the league? Don’t say Larry Bird, they had to pair him up with Magic," Villanueva said. "When was the last time a White man was single-handedly the best player in the league?"

That talking point was predictable. OutKick predicted it days after Flagg became the first overall pick out of Duke last season.

DAKICH: SPORTS MEDIA HAS CREATED AN ‘INDUSTRY’ OUT OF COMPLAINING ABOUT WHITE ATHLETES LIKE CAITLIN CLARK

For the past three to four years, several former Black players comfortably expressed belittling views of White players.

The hysteria surrounding Caitlin Clark began with the claim that her popularity and stardom resulted from "White privilege." Black players have called Luka Doncic a "bitch ass white boy" on the court. ESPN analyst Kendrick Perkins falsely accused NBA MVP voters of favoring Nikola Jokic because he is white, likely costing him the award in 2023.

More recently, Stephen A. Smith claimed a team could not win a championship built around white players. Former broadcaster Mark Jones has posted several bigoted messages about Jokic. Gilbert Arenas has joked about exiling white players from the league.

ESPN has published several articles framing Jokic, Clark, and Doncic as "great white hopes," despite the evidence to the contrary.

The pattern is obvious. Anti-white bigotry has become accepted and, at times, rewarded in public discourse. It has been normalized since 2020.

Notice Villanueva’s wording: The NBA is "a Black league, right?"

STEPHEN A SMITH SHOWS HIS PRIVILEGE BY MOCKING LAKERS' ROSTER FOR HAVING TOO MANY 'WHITE DUDES'

That view echoes comments from Arenas and others who refer to the NBA as "our" league. These Black players appear territorial about the sport and seem threatened when white players succeed.

For context, consider what activist and social media influencer Dr. Umar Johnson said about Eminem in 2023. Johnson claimed Eminem should be excluded from the conversation about the greatest rappers of all time because of his skin color.

"No non-African can ever be the best of anything African. It’s an insult to the ancestors. It’s an insult to the race and it’s an insult to every black person."

Johnson then claimed the black community should never have allowed Eminem into hip-hop.

"Eminem has all the privileges of a white male and all the privileges of being in the hip hop community, so we got to be careful about letting non-Africans into our community."

That is the message Black players send about White basketball players: Basketball is their sport. White people are merely their guests.

Of course, the premise is illogical. Basketball is not a black space. A White man created it. No sport or musical genre belongs to any race in America.

The popularity of both White and Black athletes and entertainers makes that clear. Normal Americans like Eminem for the same reasons they like Tupac, Biggie, or Jay Z. They like Jokic, Clark, Doncic, and Flagg for the same reasons they like LeBron James, Michael Jordan, and Kobe Bryant.

Unfortunately, people with the largest platforms too often promote an isolated worldview in which race determines who deserves admiration, legitimacy, and power.

Flagg could prove particularly polarizing.

The usual suspects tried dismissing Jokic and Doncic as international players. Flagg does not give them that option. He was born in Maine. He attended Duke.

His charismatic personality also gives him marketing potential that Jokic and Doncic lacked.

If Flagg emerges as a true face of the post-LeBron NBA, expect the race idolaters to react accordingly. They will resist him and diminish him with the usual racial buzzwords. They will cast his supporters as racists and sellouts.

Sound familiar?

Of course, it does. It's the response every great white basketball player now receives.

For Flagg, Villanueva's comments were just the beginning.

item.title: JACKSON THOMPSON: Maine girls speak out about facing trans athlete as state grapples with issue
item.description: Two Maine high school girls describe "crushing disappointment" competing against transgender athletes as their attorney files a Title IX complaint.
item.content:encoded:
Two Maine high school girls spoke out Monday about competing against transgender athletes, describing "crushing disappointment" and urging officials to protect their opportunities as their attorney announced plans for a federal civil rights complaint.

Reagan Wilson, a junior at Fryeburg Academy, and Morgan Clark, a junior and varsity soccer captain at Windham High School, addressed a news conference at the Maine State House in Augusta alongside advocates seeking a statewide vote on sex-based eligibility rules.

"Many girls and women are discovering the crushing disappointment that comes from being beaten in their own sports by males who should have never been allowed to compete in the first place," Wilson said.

TRANSGENDER ATHLETES HAVE TAKEN 2,293 CHAMPIONSHIP SPOTS FROM BIOLOGICAL WOMEN, NEW RESEARCH FINDS

Wilson, who said she has competed in swimming, cross-country, indoor and outdoor track, soccer and softball, described facing transgender competitors across multiple seasons.

"During my cross-country season, I competed against a biological male in many of my races. Most recently, I competed against a male playing on an all-girls soccer team," she said.

"This is unacceptable and has deprived me and so many other girls of equal opportunity to compete and win."

Clark, who said she has played soccer in Maine since she was 4, described the issue moving from something she encountered online to something affecting her own team.

COLORADO SCHOOL PARENTS SOUND ALARM AFTER DAUGHTERS WERE CUT FROM VOLLEYBALL TEAM WHILE TRANS ATHLETE PLAYS

"Last year, this sort of thing was something I only saw online, but now it’s something that I’m seeing in my own field," Clark said. "If it can happen to me, it can happen to you."

Clark pointed to an October tie against a team whose results had improved substantially over the previous season.

"In October, our team tied against a team we’ve easily outranked in past years, a team with a male athlete," she said.

Windham played South Portland to a 1-1 draw on Oct. 1. The Portland Press Herald reported that South Portland finished the previous season 3-9-2 and 14th in the regional Heal point standings.

At Monday’s news conference, Alliance Defending Freedom attorney Tavia Bruxellas McAlister said the organization would file a Title IX complaint that day on the girls’ behalf with the U.S. Department of Education’s Office for Civil Rights.

The draft seeks an investigation of the Maine Department of Education, Maine Principals’ Association, South Portland School Department and Windham Raymond School District, along with changes to eligibility policies and remedies for alleged past violations.

item.title: 'The View' host Sara Haines lauds Haley Stevens' 'brave' endorsement of Mike Rogers
item.description: Sara Haines called Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens' cross-party endorsement of Mike Rogers "brave," pushing back on those who labeled the move as a betrayal.
item.content:encoded:
"The View" co-host Sara Haines defended Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., during a discussion on Monday about the Democrat's decision to endorse Michigan Republican U.S. Senate candidate Mike Rogers over Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed, pushing back against critics who called the endorsement a betrayal.

Co-hosts Sunny Hostin and Ana Navarro both argued that Stevens endorsed Rogers for the wrong reasons, with Hostin saying, "Shame on her," if the move was motivated by a bruised ego. Stevens said during an interview on Sunday that it was El-Sayed's "anger" and "lack of kindness" that led her to endorse Rogers.

"I disagree. And I actually think that, although there’s a lot of Islamophobia here that are muddying the waters, there are deep concerns about his beliefs," Haines said. "Campaigning with Hasan Piker, you could not put enough room between me and that man. And we went after the Republicans for going around with Nick Fuentes, also problematic." 

"We have got to know when we denounce someone," she continued. "And if crossing party lines can be an act of conscience for Liz Cheney, I don’t know why the automatic response was that this was betrayal somehow." 

EL SAYED'S LEFT-WING ALLIES ATTACK 'EVIL' STEVENS AFTER BOMBSHELL ROGERS ENDORSEMENT

Haines, a registered independent, said Stevens' decision was "brave."

"Integrity is not just backing your party when you support your party," the co-host added. "The real test is backing them when it costs you something. I keep hearing, 'Donald Trump is so dangerous,' and that is true, but that can’t end every conversation we have about what we’re willing to accept on our own sides." 

"Honestly, the hateful rhetoric and demeaning language, I don’t have to agree with a candidate on everything at all, and compromise is absolutely necessary, but you cannot loan your loyalty and support out to a party," Haines continued. "They must earn it every single time. And that’s why this was actually a very brave thing for her to do."

FORMER RIVAL DODGES FULL-THROATED EL-SAYED ENDORSEMENT AFTER BITTER SENATE PRIMARY

Democratic strategist Kaivan Shroff told Fox News Digital in a statement, "Haines’s defense is hard to square with the facts. I was one of the early Democrats who said El-Sayed needed to put real distance between himself and Hasan Piker. And he did. He said Piker did not speak for his campaign, stopped campaigning with him, and reportedly even called him directly to say his rhetoric was hurting the campaign and counterproductive. That all happened well before Haley Stevens’s last-minute endorsement." 

"So Haines is using an issue El-Sayed already addressed to excuse this wild switch-up, while openly acknowledging the Islamophobia on the other side and then instantly brushing past it," he added.

Shroff argued that Haines was treating hate from one side as disqualifying, but not the other, and said, "That is not principled, balanced, or reasonable. It is just a glaring double standard."

Co-host Whoopi Goldberg brought up the timing of the endorsement as Haines argued that El-Sayed had also told Stevens he did not want her to campaign with him.

Navarro reiterated that she believed Stevens' decision was motivated by El-Sayed's reluctance to have her at the event.

HALEY STEVENS' FIANCE HAMMERS EL-SAYED, SAYS HE'LL VOTE FOR ROGERS

Fellow co-host Alyssa Farah Griffin said that Stevens had raised "real issues" about antisemitism.

Griffin also compared Stevens endorsing Rogers with Liz Cheney endorsing former Vice President Kamala Harris earlier in the segment.

"We shouldn’t just praise independents when Liz Cheney breaks with Republicans, because she thinks that’s the principled position. If this woman feels this is the principled position for her, she has every right to do that," Griffin said.

Fox News Digital reached out to the El-Sayed and Rogers campaigns for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

Shroff argued the Cheney comparison did not hold up, telling Fox News Digital, "Cheney crossed party lines because of Trump’s conduct and her stated concerns about democracy. Stevens, by contrast, says she is crossing party lines because she cannot tolerate hate, yet she is endorsing Mike Rogers in a race where anti-Muslim hate has been Rogers’s central campaign strategy."

"Moreover, Haley still maintains that Republicans — folks like Mike Rogers — are allowing Trump to act as a ‘dictator.’ It just doesn’t add up any way you try," he said.

item.title: Battleground Dem touts bipartisan record, but can’t name single issue she’d work with Trump on
item.description: Democratic Senate candidate Peggy Flanagan touted her bipartisan record but couldn't name one Trump policy she'd support, citing "continued grift."
item.content:encoded:
A Democratic Senate candidate in Minnesota touted her bipartisan record Sunday but could not name a single issue she would work with President Donald Trump on, instead accusing his administration of "continued grift."

The exchange came as Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan, Minnesota’s Democratic Senate nominee, campaigns against Republican Michele Tafoya in a race Republicans see as a rare opportunity to flip a traditionally blue state. Flanagan’s answer underscored the sharply partisan nature of the Minnesota race, where she has cast Tafoya as a rubber stamp for Trump and pledged to oppose the administration at nearly every turn.

"I just want to be really clear that I’ve got a long track record of working with folks on the other side of the aisle," Flanagan told Fox News' Bill Melugin when asked if there were any policies she could see herself working with Trump on. Flanagan pointed to her work at the Children’s Defense Fund–Minnesota and her time in the Minnesota Legislature, where she served alongside a Republican majority and helped pass bipartisan legislation, as evidence of her ability to work across the aisle.

"I think that, you know, that proves that I have the ability to work with folks," she continued.

PEGGY FLANAGAN DEMANDS EXPANDING THE SUPREME COURT AND ABOLIHING ICE

Flanagan’s bipartisan pitch comes against the backdrop of a campaign built around opposing Trump’s agenda. She has called for dismantling ICE, passing Medicare for All, and reversing the administration’s Medicaid and SNAP cuts, while accusing Trump of using the presidency to enrich himself.

"Right now, I’m deeply concerned about the Trump administration, the continued grift, making money hand over fist directly from the Oval Office," she continued in her response to Melugin on whether she would work with Trump on anything.

The Democratic Senate candidate went on to tell Melugin that what she has been "hearing" on the campaign trail is that voters want someone who will be a "check" on Trump, not his ally.

"They’re interested in whether people are going to be a check on this guy, and roll back some of the devastating cuts and impacts on Minnesota," Flanagan concluded in her answer about working with Trump. "That’s the place I’m going to start."

Flanagan is facing Republican Michele Tafoya, a former NFL sideline reporter who has turned the race into a referendum on the massive fraud scandal that unfolded under the Walz administration. Tafoya has argued that Flanagan, who served as Walz’s No. 2 as lieutenant governor, should share responsibility for the scandal, while also tying her opponent to progressive positions, including Medicare for All and dismantling ICE.

MN SENATE CANDIDATE RIPPED FOR BLAMING WALZ FOR FRAUD DESPITE BEING HIS #2: 'KNOWS SHE'S COOKED'

The race has become unexpectedly competitive after Tafoya narrowed the gap in Minnesota, prompting Fox News to shift its rating from "Likely Democrat" to "Lean Democrat."

"The more that Minnesotans learn about me and my opponent and see what my opponent has failed to do over the last eight years alongside [Democratic Gov.] Tim Walz, they're understanding Minnesota needs change. We need fresh ideas, we need an independent thinker and they're jumping on board," Tafoya said in a Fox News Digital interview.

Flanagan has repeatedly tied Tafoya to Trump, whose approval ratings are well underwater in Minnesota.

"Michele Tafoya is all in for Donald Trump — and he's all in for her," Flanagan said last month in a social media post.

But Tafoya appears to be putting some daylight between herself and Trump, as she highlights her support for abortion rights.

"I’m a pro-choice Republican not afraid to stand up to my party," Tafoya says in a new campaign commercial. "When Trump is right, I will work with him. When he is wrong, I will stand up for Minnesota."

While the ad drew opposition from some Republicans, including Mercedes Schlapp, a senior fellow at the Conservative Political Action Conference, Trump subsequently signaled support for Tafoya at an Ohio rally he headlined.

"You have to vote for Michele Tafoya, who’s a very respected person," the president said.

Fox News Digital's Paul Steinhauser contributed to this report.

item.title: Kirby Smart clarifies comments after taking shot at how much college football players are making
item.description: Kirby Smart suggested Georgia Bulldogs players may lack the hunger of past championship teams now that NIL money rivals what he earned until 40.
item.content:encoded:
Several years into the name, image, and likeness era, college football fans are now familiar with most of the resulting changes happening across the sport.

Parity within the major conferences is rapidly increasing, with the gaps between teams dropping dramatically. Players who used to commit to sit on the bench at Alabama under Nick Saban or Ohio State under Ryan Day are now bringing in bigger paydays to start at smaller schools. For good reason.

The combination of NIL and the transfer portal has made rebuilding a program overnight more realistic than it's ever been. Curt Cignetti turned the Indiana Hoosiers from an also-ran into an undefeated, National Championship-winning behemoth in just two seasons. Bob Chesney came to UCLA from James Madison and overnight, made the Bruins into a legitimate College Football Playoff contender, sitting at No. 5 in the latest Associated Press Top 25 poll late into the season.

THE CIGNETTI EFFECT IS REAL: INDIANA FOOTBALL SPARKS AN UNBELIEVABLE 'REVIVAL' IN BLOOMINGTON

But Georgia Bulldogs head coach Kirby Smart may have tacitly admitted to another result from the NIL era: a lack of motivation and aggression for the week-in, week-out grind of major conference college football.

After the Bulldogs easily handled the Florida Gators 27-8, Smart was asked about the number of injuries his team is dealing with, and whether playing a tough SEC schedule could contribute to it. And his answer was revealing about the state of modern college football, particularly with the amount of money that's now floating around it.

"Everybody is practicing less, but everybody’s getting injured more," he said.

"I think about the teams we had in ’21 and ’22, and how physical they were and how they practiced. We can’t even get close to that now," Smart added. "If it’s a different culture that guys don’t want to as much, I don’t know. They were definitely hungrier, because there was a motivation to make it. A lot of these guys, honestly, they make more than I did until I was 40. It’s just a different day and age."

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

It's an important insight that may have been obvious, but is frequently unsaid. Players may not feel the need to improve as much as they used to, because they're not fighting for the NFL payday down the road, they're already making significant money. It's human nature, and likely true, but it's one of the perhaps unexpected ancillary outcomes of players now being able to earn money for their contributions.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Still, Smart's comments received some blowback, with some adding that Smart's doing pretty well financially, and that coaches have frequently displayed a financially-motivated lack of loyalty or commitment to stick with their teams. If they can benefit from the money being generated by college football, why shouldn't the players putting themselves on the line benefit as well?

Unsurprisingly, he clarified those comments on Monday, saying he thinks it's "awesome" that young athletes are able to earn money in college sports now.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"I don’t want to come across as whining," he explained. "I think it’s awesome that players are getting paid. I wish they were being paid when I played because then maybe I wouldn’t have had to get a $5,000 job for the summer trying to work. But that is none of my concern. It is more long-term effect of earning power, what is the value of a dollar, do I actually know how hard it is to go out in the real world, and gotta go work for $60,000? That outlook can be tough on guys. But the earning power they have while they’re here, more power to them."

Again, it's an obvious fact that 18-year-olds now able to make that much money, or far, far, more is going to have some other side effects. Motivation being one of them. But like all jobs and careers, if they fail to live up to expectations, because of a lack of motivation, it can all change in the blink of an eye.

Smart added that it's now even more important to evaluate how a player will respond to making that kind of money, and whether it'll impact their ability to contribute moving forward.

"That still is an art in recruiting and decision-making: Are you recruiting the right kinds of kids that will not be affected by that," Smart said. "We used to deal with that all the time when I was at Alabama, when you’d have an (NFL) scout come in and say, ‘Well, is him being a first-round pick or second-round pick going to change him?’ That’s your job to decide that, not mine.

"Well, now it’s our job to decide as coaches. Do you have the right kind of people in your program who will be motivated for the team, and the culture of the program?"

The broader point, he added, was about the change in roster limits also impacting the ability to practice with more physicality. When the 2025 House settlement limited rosters to 105 players instead of effectively unlimited, coaches were less willing to go all out in practice and risk injuries. That, Smart believes, is part of the change to college football.

Maybe it's both. Maybe it's none of it, and it's just random variance. It's hard to know, in the modern era, with how many changes there are seemingly week-to-week. Given the chaos this season has brought already, at least the increase in parity has made for more exciting television.

item.title: JACKSON THOMPSON: Sophie Cunningham says she hired '24/7' security amid claim of FBI intervention
item.description: Sophie Cunningham says she hired 24/7 security that will travel with her, revealing the precaution on her "No Hesitation" podcast amid stalking concerns.
item.content:encoded:
Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham says she has hired security to travel with her around the clock, revealing a new precaution after recently describing concerns involving stalkers.

"I’ve definitely hired security," Cunningham said on her "No Hesitation" podcast with basketball trainer Drew Hanlen. "And they’re going to start traveling with me actually next week, 24/7."

Cunningham said the attention has spread well beyond the places where basketball fans previously recognized her.

"Now it’s like it doesn’t matter what state, what city," she said. "It’s everywhere."

The disclosure follows her appearance on Theo Von’s "This Past Weekend" podcast, where she said she believed the FBI was watching approximately 20 people over concerns involving her. Cunningham did not identify those individuals or explain the agency’s involvement. Her estimate and description of the FBI’s role have not been independently verified.

JACKSON THOMPSON: SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM CLAIMS FBI IS WATCHING 20 PEOPLE FOR HER, ON WNBA ANTHEM CONTROVERSY

In June, Indiana prosecutors charged Kevin Singh with felony stalking and intimidation and misdemeanor harassment in a case involving Cunningham. According to court documents cited by The Associated Press, Cunningham told investigators that the unwanted contact had caused her to have nightmares and stay home more frequently. The charges were allegations.

On "No Hesitation," Hanlen brought up her earlier stalking comments while asking how her increased visibility had changed daily life. He said he also receives hostile messages over his association with her.

Cunningham described online critics as people with "so much hatred in their heart," but said the larger adjustment has been figuring out how to maintain an ordinary routine.

"You have to kind of find a balance of getting away and making sure that you’re filling up your own cup," she said.

She said she remains willing to take photographs and sign autographs, but has started asking people to wait until she finishes eating.

"After I’m done eating, like I will sign whatever you want. I will take whatever picture you want," she said. "But right when you say yes to one person, I’m not kidding. It’s like a revolving door. It is non-stop."

Even trips home can leave her feeling she has spent more time entertaining strangers than visiting relatives, she said.

FEVER 2026 TIMELINE: HOW CAITLIN CLARK, SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM AND RIVALS LIKELY CHANGED THE WNBA FOREVER

"I would say the boundaries is probably the biggest thing that you have to learn," Cunningham said.

The episode also featured Cunningham taking another shot at the WNBA’s selection process for its 3-point contest.

Asked whether she would rather win that competition or "Dancing with the Stars," Cunningham chose the television show while questioning whether her shooting could earn her a contest invitation.

"I think with a three-point competition, it’s just like so clearly like political. They’re going to choose random people," she said. "So, it doesn’t matter how good I do, I probably will never get chosen for that."

Cunningham shot 41.9% from 3-point range during the 2026 regular season and was not among the six players announced for July’s contest. The WNBA’s announcement highlighted the selected players’ rankings in made 3-pointers, with all six ranking in the top 10 entering play July 21.

Cunningham did not specify what she meant by "political" or identify a particular person responsible for her exclusion.

She also called for a tougher approach to coaching after Hanlen suggested some coaches do not push young female players as hard as their male counterparts.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"Bring back hard coaching," Cunningham said.

She credited demanding coaches who cared about their players and refused to let them fall short of their potential, while arguing athletes need to accept correction.

"You can’t expect to be great and reach your fullest potential if you can’t handle someone correcting you," she said.

"I do think that coaches are too soft on athletes nowadays," Cunningham added.

"Athletes, take the ownership," she said. "It’s okay for someone to chew your ass a little bit. That’s part of it because that’s what makes athletes great."

item.title: Charley Hull dumps out SI swimsuit content from a boat, NFL player whiffs & college football's growing problem
item.description: Miami Dolphins rookie Chris Johnson's stunning sack whiff on Drake Maye left fans stunned, while college football attendance woes keep growing.
item.content:encoded:
'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com.

How we doing, folks? Let's start this week — and this month — with a quick pulse check.

Halloween is behind us. October is, sadly, behind us. We fell back yesterday morning. We're now less than 24 hours out from the midterms.

Down here in Florida, it literally has not stopped raining since Saturday night. I've lived through dozens of hurricanes and millions of summer storms in my 30 years in the Sunshine State, and I've never seen anything quite like this.

Just constant rain. Every road is flooded. My yard and the lake behind me are indistinguishable at this point. I have to use four-wheel drive to get down my dirt road, and even then, it's dicey.

As for tomorrow's election ...

So far today — and it's noon at the time of this writing — I've received 14 different texts and three calls. Some folks think Florida is turning blue. Others think we'll have this thing wrapped up by dinnertime.

My official prediction, as OutKick's unofficial Florida guy: We'll stay red, but it won't be the landslide we've grown accustomed to. On a concerned scale of 1-10, I'm around a 4.6 right now.

I was 0 in 2024, and 2 in 2022 for reference.

Anyway, let's talk sports for a bit and leave all that other nonsense behind.

Welcome to a Monday Nightcaps — the one where LPGA star Charley Hull starts Thanksgiving month on a boat in Ibiza. What a life!

SPORTS ILLUSTRATED ADDS CHARLEY HULL TO ITS SWIMSUIT ROSTER, NASCAR'S NOSEDIVE & DO WE HAVE ANTHEM FATIGUE?

What else? I've got the worst sack attempt you'll ever see out of Miami yesterday, a very clear attendance problem brewing in college football and wait till you see the ... reception ... the WNBA champs got in Golden State last night.

I know I know — I said Friday I was done talking about anything non-Sophie Cunningham in the WNBA, but this is incredible. It's worth breaking the rule.

Trust me.

OK, grab you a sandwich for tomorrow's National Sandwich Day, and settle in for a Monday 'Cap!

Here's some free advice ... don't overlook Panera in the sandwich game. That's right.

Panera.

PANERA BREAD GRABS TOP HONORS FOR AMERICA'S HIGHEST-RATED FAST-FOOD BREAKFAST ITEM

After two days of rain, I needed to get out of the house today. I couldn't take it anymore. So, I hopped in my boat and drove down the street to the Panera to work. I come here once in a while, mainly because the WiFi is better than most and I can get a cup of coffee for $2.

Anyway, I've dabbled in lunch a few times over the past few months, and I gotta say — Panera sandwiches are top shelf. People like to give Panera crap for being too pricey or too corporate, and I usually agree with that crowd. But not here. They have a new French Ciabatta Dipper out right now that'll blow your mind.

Not an ad, by the way (although I wouldn't mind if it was). Just figured I'd help everyone out on this first Monday of November.

Good? Good!

Now, let's get this week started with Miami Dolphins rookie corner Chris Johnson whiffing on a sack so badly yesterday, I thought my TV glitched.

Seriously:

Goodness gracious. I've watched it 50 times and I still can't believe it's real. Heck, I watched it LIVE and seriously thought I was missing something. I saw him come around the end unblocked, and thought Drake Maye was about to die.

At worst, it was going to be a sack. At best, I figured it'd be a strip-sack going the other way for a Dolphins touchdown. There was no scenario in which Johnson ... missed. Amazing.

Now, to be fair, he's a rookie. He's also had a really good season, including a great play later in the drive that should've been fourth down stop, but the refs stink so they ruled it a first down. It wasn't, but that's neither here nor there.

Regardless, it was an all-time whiff. I've watched football for 30 years. I don't recall seeing a whiff quite like that.

Dolphins football in 2026, I reckon. Tank on!

Next? I've said all year that I think college football has been a superior product to the NFL this season, and I still believe that. This upcoming Saturday is shaping up to be the greatest Saturday slate of all time.

BUT ... as my old boss once told the entire company at a Christmas town hall before laying off half the office six months later, "I see some storm clouds on the horizon."

Holy cow. I'm not going to share every post from that thread because I don't want to bog us down, but my goodness, it's ugly.

Some of those empty stadiums are completely understandable. Maryland, for instance. The Terps stink, they just fired their coach, and they have no business being in the Big Ten. I get that one. Why in the world would anyone go to a Maryland game?

But, it wasn't just the bad teams ...

LOOK at the crowd for an actual ranked matchup between Texas Tech and Arizona:

Or, for PENN STATE:

Lordy. As I usually do on a Monday, I'd like to open this up for debate. What do you think is going on with college football attendance? TV ratings are good. The product on the field has been good. What's the deal?

Me? I think the regular season has been watered down because of the playoffs, and I think — above all — folks have no real connection to these players anymore. These big programs don't have any more homegrown talent. It's all transfer portal kids. And they're all richer than most fans in attendance.

The connection has been lost, and that connection is what made college football so great.

Let me know! Zach.Dean@OutKick.com.

OK, on the way out, let's all congratulate the WNBA champion Golden State Valkyries!

I mean, it's just the perfect way to put a bow on this WNBA season. Listen to that crowd! They genuinely could not care less if they tried. Even the insufferable PA announcer is BEGGING them to get louder, and it's pointless.

What a moment. What a season.

OK, that's it for today. Good start to the week, folks. Good start to the month. Let's all suffer through these next 48 hours together, and put this election in the rearview.

On the way out, here's Charley Hull dumping out some SI Swimsuit content from a boat in Ibiza.

Let's have a big week.

item.title: Multiple people killed, others injured in shooting near California beach
item.description: The Monterey County Sheriff's Office said multiple people were killed in a shooting along Jetty Road in Moss Landing shortly after midnight.
item.content:encoded:
Multiple people were killed and others injured in a shooting near a California beach early Monday, authorities said.

The Monterey County Sheriff's Office said in a press release that deputies and detectives responded to a shooting along Jetty Road in Moss Landing shortly after midnight.

"There are multiple fatalities and casualties confirmed," the sheriff's office said.

North County Fire Protection Chief Jess Cortez said crews found two people with gunshot wounds to the chest and another person with minor injuries, according to FOX 2 KTVU.

ONE DEAD, 6 INJURED AFTER GUNFIRE ERUPTS AT UNSANCTIONED CALIFORNIA PARTY THAT DREW HUNDREDS: SHERIFF

The two gunshot victims were pronounced dead at the scene, while the injured person was taken to a hospital, Cortez told the station.

Authorities have not said how many people were killed or injured in total or provided details about what led to the shooting.

California State Parks Police closed Jetty Road and Moss Landing State Beach at the request of the sheriff's office as the investigation continued.

SHOOTING AT FLORIDA BEACH 'TEEN TAKEOVER' LEAVES 17-YEAR-OLD HOSPITALIZED WITH GUNSHOT WOUND

"There is no active threat to the Moss Landing Community at this time," the sheriff's office said. 

"This is an active investigation, and no further information will be released at this time."

State Sen. John Laird called the shooting an "unspeakable horror" and offered his condolences to those affected.

FLORIDA WOMAN, 70, OPENS FIRE INSIDE PORT ORANGE POLICE DEPARTMENT LOBBY, CHIEF SAYS

"Over the weekend, there were numerous reports of shooting deaths across the country. This unspeakable horror has also hit home on the Central Coast, with reports of multiple fatalities just after midnight today in Moss Landing," Laird said in a statement. 

"The pain and suffering of all those impacted is impossible to measure and my heart goes out to everyone. Thank you to the Monterey County Sheriff and team for its management of this devastating situation."

The Monterey County Sheriff's office could not immediately be reached for comment.

item.title: Boat explodes during tourist outing as fire sends captain, others scrambling into water
item.description: Dramatic video captures the moment a snorkeling boat exploded near Nusa Penida, forcing four tourists and their guide to jump into the water to save themselves.
item.content:encoded:
Four foreign tourists and their guide were forced to jump into the water after their snorkeling boat exploded and caught fire near Bali, Indonesia, according to authorities.

The boat, which was on a snorkeling excursion, exploded and caught fire on Thursday in the waters of Gamat Bay off Nusa Penida, according to a statement from the Klungkung Regency Police, a local police agency in Bali.

The boat had planned stops at Manta Bay, Crystal Bay and Gamat Bay.

3 KILLED, 5 INJURED AT POPULAR TOURIST HOT SPOT AFTER ROCKS SUDDENLY TUMBLE DOWN

About an hour into the excursion, the boat was preparing to leave Gamat Bay when "a loud explosion was heard from the end of the boat," police said.

"The explosion is thought to have come from a battery component attached to the boat," the statement said.

"The flames then appeared so that the guide and four foreign guests spontaneously jumped into the sea to save themselves."

Around 2:50 p.m., a passing boat rescued the passengers and crew members, Senior Commissioner Rina Isriana Dewi, said the chief of the public information subdivision of the Bali Police Public Relations division. 

CRUISE PASSENGERS FACE BLOCKED ACCESS AS ANGRY PROTESTERS SET BARRICADES ON FIRE

Police reported that everyone survived, though the boat captain suffered serious burns to his legs.

"In this incident, all foreign national passengers and boat crew were successfully evacuated safely," the translated statement said.

The captain was later taken to the emergency room at Gema Santhi Regional Hospital for treatment, according to ANTARA News, the official national news agency of Indonesia.

The boat, named Naomi, had undergone routine repairs and maintenance before the incident, authorities said. 

The exact cause of the explosion and fire remains under investigation.

An island roughly 15 miles southeast of Bali, Nusa Penida is known for its crystal-clear waters, coastal cliffs and popular snorkeling spots.

Tourism in Bali has grown in recent years, with the island welcoming nearly 7 million foreign tourists in 2025, a nearly 10% increase from the previous year, according to Indonesia's official statistics agency.

Other recent boating fires and explosions have also put travelers in danger.

Last year, a couple vacationing in England jumped into the River Thames to rescue six people, including four children, after a boat exploded and caught fire.

item.title: Michael Wilbon announces indefinite leave from ESPN, 'PTI' due to ‘multiple health issues’
item.description: Michael Wilbon announced he's stepping away from "PTI" and NBA duties at ESPN due to multiple health issues, saying he should have listened sooner.
item.content:encoded:
Michael Wilbon is taking an indefinite leave of absence from ESPN due to "multiple health issues," the legendary sports commentator announced in a statement Monday.

"This isn’t retirement, but it is a trip to the injured list. Hopefully not an extended one. Struggles with multiple health issues in recent months lead me to take an indefinite leave of absence from my PTI and NBA duties at ESPN and ABC," Wilbon began.

"Probably, I should have listened to medical professionals and people closest to me, yep Kornheiser included, who saw worrisome signs in recent years that suggested I take time away earlier. But I didn’t."

Wilbon did not specify which medical issues he is facing. He has previously spoken about managing diabetes and complications from the disease.

He co-hosted "PTI" from his home in Arizona last Monday but was absent for the rest of the week.

Most importantly, we want to send our best wishes to Michael Wilbon. Speaking personally, it has been an honor to get to know him professionally. OutKick has had the pleasure of interviewing Wilbon on several occasions.

He is one of the greatest sportswriters and commentators of this generation. And it's not cliché to say he's an even greater person.

One would be hard-pressed to find someone in this industry more universally respected by his peers, viewers, readers, and contemporaries.

Scott Van Pelt provided OutKick a comment on Wilbon's importance to the industry as both a professional and a person:

"I grew up reading him in the Post, never imagined we’d be colleagues and friends. Because he’s old school in the best of ways, he’d roll his eyes at the idea he’s revered by all of us, but he is. I hope he sees the outpouring and allows it to land in a way that serves as fuel to feel a bit better," Van Pelt said.

Other sports media commentators wished Wilbon well Monday, referencing his influence on them:

Clay Travis: "Get well. One of the all time greats at writing and TV."

Josh Pate: "I always learn something when Michael Wilbon talks…here’s a big get well soon to someone I hope is around for years to come 🫡."

John Buccigross: "The charm and warmth of this man is astounding. There's nothing quite like him. Rest your mind and bones Mr. Wilbon."

Dan Wetzel: "Best of health to Michael Wilbon, whose talent, intelligence and work ethic have made him one of the greatest sports columnists AND sports commentators of all time."

ESPN Chairman Jimmy Pitaro also issued a statement in support of Wilbon.

"Michael and his family have ESPN’s full support as he takes time away to focus on his health and well-being. He’s an important member of our ESPN team and widely respected by his peers, sports fans and so many others throughout our industry.

"We are here for Michael every step of the way and look forward to welcoming him back whenever he is ready."

Honestly, knowing Wilbon just a little and having followed his career, he would despise how long we have already spent writing about his announcement. He will be back.

Well before.

item.title: Dangerous mosquito-borne virus surges in popular US state as cases reach highest levels in decades
item.description: Florida's dengue fever outbreak has reached 485 locally acquired cases, with Tampa Bay accounting for 95% of infections and emergency declarations issued.
item.content:encoded:
Florida health officials have confirmed 485 locally acquired cases of dengue fever this year, as the state grapples with its largest outbreak in decades.

Between Oct. 18 and Oct. 24, state surveillance logged 60 new infections, with the Tampa Bay area accounting for roughly 95% of all locally acquired cases recorded statewide, according to the Florida Department of Health.

The surge prompted emergency declarations in Hillsborough, Pasco and Pinellas counties in late September, allowing for faster purchasing and spraying and requests for state and federal reimbursement. Hillsborough County has since extended its state of local emergency amid ongoing transmission.

DENGUE FEVER OUTBREAK TRIGGERS STATES OF EMERGENCY IN 3 SOUTHERN COUNTIES

The locally acquired infections are separate from more than 300 travel-associated dengue cases reported in Florida this year.

The Florida Mosquito Control Association said mosquito abatement teams are stepping up targeted ground spraying, aerial applications and localized property inspections.

Dengue is a viral illness transmitted primarily through the bite of infected Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus mosquitoes. The virus can cause fever, severe muscle and joint pain, nausea, rash and, in severe cases, dangerous complications or death, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

Unlike many mosquito species that bite mostly at dawn and dusk, the mosquitoes carrying dengue feed aggressively during daytime hours and thrive in humid residential environments.

DEADLY MOSQUITO-BORNE VIRUS CLAIMS FIRST LIFE IN MAJOR US CITY AS CASES SPREAD

"The Aedes mosquitoes that can transmit dengue are active during the day and thrive in warm, humid environments like those found in Florida," an entomologist spokesperson at the SC Johnson Center for Insect Science and Family Health previously told Fox News Digital.

"Staying aware of local mosquito activity and consistently protecting against bites are important steps people can take to help reduce their risk."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

Public health officials emphasize that Aedes mosquitoes are "container breeders," requiring as little as a tablespoon of standing water to lay eggs. Officials urge residents to inspect yards weekly and drain or cover birdbaths, gutters, planters, discarded tires and outdoor containers.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Health authorities recommend taking the following additional precautions.

Most people infected with dengue experience mild or no symptoms, typically recovering within two weeks, according to Mayo Clinic.

When symptoms do occur, they usually surface four to 10 days after an infectious bite. Severe dengue can progress rapidly within 24 to 48 hours after the initial fever drops.

Warning signs include persistent vomiting, severe abdominal pain, difficulty breathing, mucosal bleeding and extreme lethargy.

Anyone experiencing those signs should seek emergency medical care immediately.
